For here, as in many other places, whatever profit is collected returns in its entirety to the King. Adjacent to this place are the workshops of the goldsmiths, whose consul keeps the seal and the dies for the coins. In Fez, neither a ring nor any other thing can be fashioned from gold or silver unless the metal has been sealed first; for they punish transgressors most severely. But once the metal is sealed, whatever is made from it is spent as if it were currency. However, the greater part of the goldsmiths who inhabit the New Fez are Jews, and they carry the gold and silver vessels to a certain place in the Old Fez, situated not far from the spice merchants, to sell them. For in Old Fez, neither gold nor silver is minted, nor are the <term>Mahumetani</term> <gloss>Muslims</gloss> permitted to practice that craft, because they have usurers who resell any silver or gold work for more than the weight warrants, although that is permitted to the Jews by the governors of the city. You may also find here some who craft vessels only for the citizens, for which they are paid wages only in proportion to their labor. That part of the city which the Royal Guards once inhabited
